name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.179.0 — The critic is out: the mocks chain now derives THEME straight off a fully approved WIREFRAMES stage, retiring the fresh-context critic pass and its ledger-pinned question producer end to end — the retired mark, reopen target, ask subcommand and answer route are all refused as unknown inputs now, the critic agent and its two dispatch sites are gone, and an assumption row is confirmed or overridden only by the human-run `ledger set`. A note a person did not type stays on disk but is never listed, grouped, counted or gated on again, and the composer's reason chips are retired in the same stroke — the textarea grows to fill the freed height. 7.178.0 — The region-note layer now owns one interaction mode at a time — idle, arming, drawing or composing, written only through setMode — with pointer capture on the overlay itself replacing three document-level listeners and a click-swallowing shield, named exits from every drag (Escape, a sub-12px release, pointercancel, lostpointercapture), and drag geometry clamped to the mock document before capture. Affordances (cursor, pointer-events, touch-action, the marking scrim) derive from the overlay's own data-mode in viewer.css instead of imperative style writes, box selection reconciles by id instead of rebuilding the layer, and reveal (scroll + pulse) fires only when a selection did not originate on the clicked box itself, with viewer.css now shipping the pulse keyframes and the has-sel dim rule the approved prototype always specified. On the review page, a framed board's note and draft cards are built by the frame but placed by the host page in its own document at full, unscaled size beside — never over — the box, so a card no longer renders unreadably small under a board's CSS scale. 7.177.0 — The replay tree is the reviewed tree: each review now records the two commits bounding what it judged as refs under refs/spec-review/<runId>/ — judged at the close row's head sha, close at the close commit — written best-effort so a failed write can never block a close. The replay harness reads that pair instead of asking which commit last touched the spec file, refuses (exit 4) a row that cannot name its own bounds, and reconstructs the pre-ref backlog only through the new run-once replay.js --backfill-pins. Setup re-derives the target's own AC coverage against the tree it assembled and exits 5 with a diagnosis rather than printing a success line over a tree the review never saw.
